rich2021Content: Original IM2021 G5 U05:L26 Book Drive is an OPTIONAL OPEN mathematical modeling project: pupils plan a school book sale, choose 3–5 source categories, select a mark-up price per type and estimate likely profit based on justified attendance and demand assumptions. It has no single source correct sales projection.

Warm-up Notice and Wonder Books for Sale uses attributed photograph by Rumman Amin CC0 Unsplash not individually downloaded/verified for reuse. Teacher asks pupils to notice real market tradeoffs and explains that higher price does not prove higher sales volume.

Activity1 Book Prices: both schools BUY science books for SOURCE $8 per book; School A SELLS at$12, School B at$12.90, yielding margins$4 and$4.90 per book. For35 books each original scenario profits are$140 and$171.50, respectively. Which school will actually sell more cannot be inferred from prices alone. If B sells10 books it earns$49 margin; A selling12 books earns$48 (ABOUT same), while13 earns$52 and at least meets$49; source asks ABOUT same, so teacher must assess reasoned interpretation instead of marking one unique quantity.

Activity2 Plan a Book Fair printed PUBLISHER COST LIST: boxed sets/collections$24.95, comic books$2.60, science books$8.00, chapter books$9.99, history books$14.49, audiobooks$20.00, activity books$4.50, reference books$12.00, Spanish-language books$6.00, biographies$6.05. Learners choose3–5 categories, decide selling prices and estimate numbers sold. There is NO fixed source volume or fixed optimal plan.

Original pupil estimates should include too-low/about-right/too-high range and assumptions for visitor volume, price, demand, school context and total net/gross profit above purchase cost. Teacher reviews arithmetic, choice ethics and uncertainty. Previous fictitious$7.25/$10.25 pricing is a mathematically valid Edulytiks extension only. The exact numeric family is limited to source two-school calculation, not the open project. There is no original source Cool-down in teacher HTML; independent Edulytiks reflection rubric is distinct.
